blocks.text: The **atmosphere** is the gaseous envelope of the Earth, layered by temperature into the **troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere**. Its composition (mostly **nitrogen and oxygen**) and the **ozone layer** make life possible.

rows: 0–~12 km; **all weather occurs here**; temp falls with height (**normal lapse rate ~6.5°C/km**).
~12–50 km; contains the **ozone layer** (absorbs UV); ideal for **jet flights**; temp rises.
**Nitrogen ~78%, Oxygen ~21%**, Argon ~0.9%, CO₂ ~0.04%; water vapour & dust variable.

items: Troposphere = weather; Stratosphere = ozone; Mesosphere = meteors burn; Ionosphere = radio reflection.

prelimsPointers: Layers (ascending) — **Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere**.
**All weather** occurs in the **Troposphere**; **normal lapse rate ~6.5°C/km**.
**Ozone layer** lies in the **Stratosphere** (absorbs UV).
**Mesosphere** — coldest; **meteors burn up** here.
**Ionosphere (thermosphere)** reflects **radio waves**; **auroras** occur here.
Composition — **Nitrogen 78%, Oxygen 21%, Argon 0.9%, CO₂ 0.04%**.
**Tropopause, Stratopause** etc. separate the layers.
mainsAngles: Describe the structure and composition of the atmosphere.

glossary.definition: The lowest atmospheric layer where all weather phenomena occur.
The stratospheric band of ozone that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
The rate of temperature decrease with height, normally ~6.5°C per km in the troposphere.

sections.heading: Elements & factors of climate; air masses & fronts

blocks.text: **Weather and climate** are described by **elements** (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, precipitation) and controlled by **factors** (latitude, altitude, distance from sea, ocean currents, relief, winds). **Air masses** and their boundaries (**fronts**) drive mid-latitude weather.

rows: **Latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents, prevailing winds, relief, slope/aspect**.
**Equatorial low, Sub-tropical high, Sub-polar low, Polar high** (4 belts pattern).
**Trade winds, Westerlies, Polar easterlies**; deflected by Coriolis.
**cP, cT, mP, mT**; fronts — **warm, cold, occluded, stationary** (weather boundaries).

items: Distinguish elements (measured) vs factors/controls (latitude, altitude, sea, currents).
Four pressure belts; three planetary winds (trades, westerlies, polar easterlies); fronts = air-mass boundaries.

prelimsPointers: **Elements of weather** — temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, precipitation.
**Factors/controls** — **latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents, winds, relief**.
Four **pressure belts** — equatorial low, sub-tropical high, sub-polar low, polar high.
**Planetary winds** — Trade winds (E), Westerlies, Polar easterlies.
**Air masses** — continental Polar (cP), maritime Tropical (mT), etc.
**Fronts** — warm, cold, occluded, stationary (boundary between two air masses).
**Temperature inversion** — temp rises with height (calm, clear nights, valleys).
mainsAngles: Distinguish the elements and controlling factors of climate.

glossary.definition: A large body of air with uniform temperature and humidity acquired from its source region.
The boundary between two contrasting air masses, along which weather forms.
A global zone of high or low pressure (e.g. equatorial low) that steers planetary winds.

blocks.text: **Atmospheric disturbances** — cyclones (tropical & temperate), thunderstorms and jet streams — produce much of the world's severe weather, while **climate change** (global warming from greenhouse gases) is altering these patterns — a topic of high current relevance.

rows: Form over warm seas (>26.5°C); **eye, eyewall**; called **cyclones (India), hurricanes (Atlantic), typhoons (Pacific)**; hit AP/Odisha coast.
Mid-latitude, front-based; bring **western disturbances** (NW India winter rain).
Fast upper-air westerlies; **sub-tropical jet** influences the Indian monsoon.
**El Nino** (warm Pacific) → weak monsoon/drought; **La Nina** → good monsoon.
**Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄), global warming, sea-level rise**; Paris Agreement, IPCC.

items: Cyclone naming by region; El Nino weakens the Indian monsoon; jet stream steers monsoon onset.
Climate change = GHGs → warming, sea-level rise; IPCC & Paris Agreement.

prelimsPointers: **Tropical cyclones** need warm seas (>26.5°C); have an **eye & eyewall**; **cyclone/hurricane/typhoon** by region.
AP's coast is highly **cyclone-prone** (Bay of Bengal, Oct-Dec).
**Western disturbances** (temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean) bring **winter rain to NW India**.
**Jet streams** — sub-tropical westerly jet influences **monsoon onset & withdrawal**.
**El Nino** (warm eastern Pacific) → **weak monsoon/drought**; **La Nina** → strong monsoon.
**Greenhouse gases** — CO₂, methane (CH₄), N₂O; cause **global warming**.
**IPCC** (assessment reports) & the **Paris Agreement (2015, 1.5-2°C)** address climate change.
mainsAngles: Discuss atmospheric disturbances and the impact of climate change on the monsoon.

glossary.definition: An intense low-pressure storm forming over warm tropical seas, called a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.
An abnormal warming of the eastern Pacific that tends to weaken the Indian monsoon.
A narrow band of fast upper-atmospheric wind that influences monsoon and mid-latitude weather.

blocks.text: The **oceans** cover ~71% of Earth and are described by their **relief (physical), salinity/temperature (chemical) and marine life (biological)** characteristics, along with **currents, tides and waves** that regulate global climate.

rows: **Continental shelf → slope → deep-sea plain (abyssal) → trench (deepest — Mariana)**; mid-oceanic ridges.
Avg **~35 ppt**; highest in enclosed seas (Dead Sea, Red Sea); lower near river mouths/poles.
Decreases with depth; **thermocline** separates warm surface from cold deep.
Warm (Gulf Stream, Kuroshio) & cold (Labrador, Humboldt); regulate coastal climate & fisheries.
**Spring tides (new/full moon), Neap tides (quarter moon)**; caused by Moon & Sun gravity.

items: Ocean relief order: shelf→slope→abyssal plain→trench (Mariana deepest); salinity ~35 ppt.
Spring tides (new/full moon, highest) vs Neap tides (quarter moon).

prelimsPointers: Oceans cover **~71%** of Earth; **continental shelf** is the richest fishing/oil zone.
**Mariana Trench (Pacific)** — deepest point (Challenger Deep).
Average ocean **salinity ~35 ppt (parts per thousand)**; highest in the **Dead Sea**.
**Thermocline** — the zone of rapid temperature decrease with depth.
**Warm currents** — Gulf Stream (Atlantic), Kuroshio (Pacific); **cold** — Labrador, Humboldt/Peru.
**Spring tides** — new & full moon (highest); **Neap tides** — first/last quarter (lowest).
Meeting of warm & cold currents creates rich **fishing grounds** (e.g. Grand Banks).
mainsAngles: Describe the physical and chemical characteristics of ocean waters.

glossary.definition: The shallow, gently sloping seabed near coasts, rich in fisheries and hydrocarbons.
The dissolved salt content of seawater, averaging ~35 parts per thousand.
The highest tide, occurring at new and full moon when Sun and Moon align.

blocks.text: Water-related hazards — **floods, tsunamis, droughts and storm surges** — cause major disasters, while **marine and continental resources** (fisheries, minerals, energy, water) are vital to the economy — both especially relevant to coastal Andhra.

rows: Seismic sea-wave (earthquake/undersea landslide); **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami** hit the AP/TN coast.
Monsoon floods; **cyclonic storm surges** on the AP-Odisha coast.
**Fisheries, offshore oil/gas (KG basin), placer minerals (monazite beach sands), salt, tidal energy**.
**Freshwater, soils, forests, minerals, groundwater** on land.

items: Tsunami (2004) & cyclonic storm surge = major AP coastal hazards; KG basin = offshore gas.
Beach-sand placer minerals (monazite) and fisheries are key marine resources.

prelimsPointers: **Tsunamis** are triggered by undersea **earthquakes**; the **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami** struck the AP/Tamil-Nadu coast.
**Storm surges** from Bay-of-Bengal cyclones flood the AP-Odisha coast.
**Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin** — major offshore **oil & natural gas** reserves.
**Beach-sand placer minerals** — **monazite (thorium), ilmenite, garnet** along the AP coast.
**Rayalaseema** — chronically drought-prone (AP).
**Tidal & wave energy, salt, fisheries** — marine resources.
**NDMA** (National Disaster Management Authority) coordinates disaster response.
mainsAngles: Assess hydrological disasters and marine resources with reference to coastal Andhra.

glossary.definition: A series of ocean waves generated by undersea earthquakes or landslides.
An abnormal rise of seawater during a cyclone that floods low-lying coasts.
Heavy minerals (e.g. monazite, ilmenite) concentrated in beach and river sands.
